quote: Criteria 1, 3 and 4 hold: the task is an upper-extremity visuomotor rotation ('participants performed 120 trials (30 cycles) in which the position of the cursor was rotated 30 clockwise relative to the central home position') with a post-exposure phase ('participants performed 48 trials (12 cycles) with the perturbation removed'), and the paper is in English. Criterion 2 fails: the study is a continuous-age population cohort in which age is never analysed as two groups — 'although all analyses were performed with age as a continuous variable' — and the only age bands ('young' = 18e45 years, N = 109; 'middle' = 46e65 years, N = 102; 'old' = 66e89 years, N = 108) are stated to be 'For illustration purposes only'. No older-versus-younger group statistics (means, SDs, group Ns for a contrast) are reported; the age effect is given only as correlations/regression coefficients (e.g., 'significant negative correlation between age and final adaptation (r(317) = 0.349 ...)').
detail: Criterion 2: the paper does not report data comparing an older group with a younger group — age is modelled as a continuous variable across a single lifespan cohort (n = 322, 18e89 years), and the three age bands shown in figures are explicitly for illustration only, with no group-level outcome values printed.

quote: Criterion 1 is met (upper-extremity visuomotor rotation: "the subsequent 11 blocks (B2–B12; adaptation period) were performed with visual feedback rotated 30° clockwise about the center of the screen"), and criterion 3 is partly met (direction error per block during the perturbation). However criterion 2 fails: the study tested a single young-adult sample only — "Eighteen participants (21.1 ± 2.5 yrs; 9 men) were recruited from the University of Michigan student population" — with no older adult group and no age-group comparison. The paper is in English.
detail: Criterion 2: the study reports no comparison of older adults with younger adults; only one young sample (mean age 21.1 ± 2.5 yrs) was tested, and individual differences were related to neuropsychological/SWM measures rather than age.

quote: Criterion 1 is met (upper-extremity visuomotor perturbation: "During the experimental trials the on-line visual feedback of the movement was rotated 45 with a \u221a2 gain."). Criterion 2 fails: the sample is a single young cohort with no older-adult group — "Thirty-two students of Louisiana State University with a mean age of 21.72 yrs (\u00b12.92 yrs; 19 females, 13 males) participated in the experiment." The study's contrasts are between hands/training conditions (R-R-R, L-L-L, L-R-L, R-L-R), not between age groups.
detail: Criterion 2: the study does not report data comparing older adults with younger adults; all participants were university students with a mean age of 21.72 yrs, and the comparisons are between hands (dominant vs non-dominant) and bilateral-transfer conditions.
